text: At the start of the season, the farmer prepares the field by ploughing and leveling the soil. He removes crop residue and checks that the land drains properly. Before planting, the farmer treats the seeds with a biological fungicide and allows them to dry. The worker then sows the treated seeds in rows and covers them lightly with soil. After sowing, the farmer irrigates the field with a drip system so that water reaches the roots. He checks the moisture each morning and avoids flooding the young crop. When the plants begin to grow, the farmer applies organic fertilizer around the crop and adds compost to improve the soil. He watches for insects and weeds. If pests are seen, the farmer controls them by spraying pesticide on the crop. The farmer removes weeds by hand and keeps the irrigation lines clear. Later, if rainfall is low, he may irrigate the field again using a sprinkler system. The farm workers do not harvest the crop while the grain is green. When the grain is mature, the farmer harvests the crop and collects the produce for storage. After harvest, the workers clean the tools and prepare the field for the next season. The farmer keeps a notebook showing the planting date, seed variety, and amount of water used. This record helps compare growth between parts of the field. Workers inspect the young plants during the week and remove weeds around each row. They place cut weeds away from the seedling beds and avoid disturbing the roots. Near maturity, the farmer stops applying fertilizer and lets the grain dry on the stalk. Workers collect the mature crop by hand and carry the produce to a dry storage room. During a break, the workers drink water. Water is essential for crop growth.

text: First, prepare the soil and remove the stones from the field. Next, treat the seeds before sowing them. After the seeds are sown, irrigate the field with drip irrigation. Do not apply fertilizer until the seedlings appear. When the seedlings are established, the farmer applies compost to the soil. If pests threaten the crop, use pesticide to control them. The farmer may harvest the crop next week, but the crop is not harvested today. Workers drink water after their work. The farmer waters the crops only when the soil is dry, and the plants receive water through a sprinkler system during hot weather. Finally, harvest the mature crop and store the grain safely. During the following days, workers watch the crop and report changes in leaf color. The farmer records each irrigation event and keeps the seed bags dry. Before the next field operation, the workers check that the tools are clean and that the paths between rows are clear. Mulch is spread over exposed soil to reduce evaporation and protect the surface. If rain arrives, the farmer postpones irrigation. When the crop is ready, workers harvest the grain and carry it to storage. They clean the equipment after use and prepare the field for another planting season. The schedule changes with soil moisture, rainfall, and crop growth, so each action is carried out only when the field conditions are suitable. The notebook helps workers coordinate their schedule, but weather and soil conditions always determine when tasks can be completed safely.
